name: Cultural and Historic Ensemble of the Solovetsky Islands
description: The Solovetsky Islands are a cluster of six islands in the White Sea of northern Russia, covering about 300 square kilometres. Monks settled here in the 15th century and built a fortress-like monastery, founded in 1436, along with several churches from the 16th to 19th centuries. People lived on the islands even earlier, and in 1923 the monastery became the Soviet Union's first Gulag prison camp.
